svg.title: TCP three-way handshake
svg.desc: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK sync both sides' sequence numbers before any data flows. x and y are each side's random initial sequence numbers (ISNs). Each ACK acknowledges the peer's ISN + 1 because a SYN consumes one sequence number. SYN and the final ACK travel on the same client-to-server edge; the segment type and its numbers are carried by the phase name. Retransmission of lost segments, simultaneous open and SYN cookies are not shown. The final phase closes the connection so the loop can restart; the FIN/ACK teardown itself is not drawn. 1. SYN seq=x: client opens at ISN x. 2. SYN-ACK seq=y ack=x+1: server confirms x, offers y. 3. ACK ack=y+1: client confirms y. 4. Established: server is open too; data flows both ways. 5. Closed: after teardown the server listens again.
